objective: Find fast English-dub anime streams through live extraction, first-frame decoding, and speech language checks.

recommendations.fastest_tested: AniWaves at 720p, via new GitHub prototype
recommendations.best_tested_1080p: ReAnime with its embedded English audio track explicitly selected
recommendations.ready_dub_fallback: AnimeKai, then HiAnime; they share the tested Zoko backend

method.repeated_measurement: Three rounds of three episodes for AniWaves, AnimeKai, HiAnime and AniKage, rotated order and one decoder at a time. ReAnime English was retested separately for the same nine cases.
method.first_frame_definition: Wall time until FFmpeg emits a positive decoded frame counter, progress interval 50 ms. Includes network setup, demuxing and decoding; is not a visible-player paint measurement.

decode_configuration.output: null muxer, decoded video and audio

language_detection.evidence: Detected English speech with >=0.9 confidence on each of the three titles for recommended routes. ReAnime eng audio and Senshi en audio explicitly selected. Probabilistic speech detection, not an exhaustive dub catalog audit.

method.source_lookup_comparability: SDK timing includes TMDB metadata through a fresh CLI process. GitHub prototypes were supplied title/year/AniList metadata and timed source resolution only; shared lookup caches were cleared between AniWaves rounds. First-frame-after-URL timing is directly comparable as a playback pipeline measurement, but resolution totals are not identical application architectures.
method.quality_comparability: AniWaves/AniKage samples are 720p; ReAnime/AnimeKai/HiAnime/Senshi samples are 1080p. Codec, bitrate, upstream caches, and network conditions differ.
method.ffmpeg: ffmpeg version n9.0.2 Copyright (c) 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers
method.privacy: No signed media URLs, cookies, keys, private headers, raw speech or transcripts in this report.

findings: AniWaves passed 9/9 repeated short decodes and 3/3 sixty-second decodes. Its raw startup was consistently below one second.
ReAnime passed 9/9 repeated English-track decodes and 3/3 sixty-second decodes. Files are multi-audio and default Japanese even when a card is labeled dub; select eng explicitly.
AnimeKai and HiAnime passed 9/9 each, but share identical tested dub stream identities. They are alternate discovery routes rather than independent playback redundancy.

The sampled AnimeGG dub candidates for Frieren and Jujutsu Kaisen contained Japanese speech and no separate English track was observed. These candidates are excluded; this is not a claim that every AnimeGG dub is wrong.
A new Anikoto prototype played the Jujutsu Kaisen candidate but speech detection favored Japanese at only 0.616 confidence. It was not accepted as confirmed English.
Senshi resolved multi-audio 1080p media, but playlists use proprietary EM3U8v1 AES-GCM wrapping. A bounded temporary local playlist adapter plus explicit en audio decoded all three samples.
AniZone supplied no dub for the test episode. AnimeOnsen and AniBD references are sub-only; excluded from the English-dub shortlist.
AniNeko current page returned no matches in the sampled scraper flow. KickAssAnime source lookups worked but sampled media did not decode on this connection.
AllAnime/MKissa metadata search worked quickly; sampled current source flows failed and the published keygen attempt returned AA_CRYPTO_STALE. Fast search alone does not prove fast playback.
AniDap download API returned 503; WCO pages returned Cloudflare 403. Neither was promoted without playback evidence.

AniStream resolved source metadata, but sampled Nexabloom/Krussdomi media failed to decode. Existing AnimeZeY/Animesuge/AnikotoTV/AllWish/AniDoor sampled routes did not produce confirmed English-dub candidates.
